messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: finally building on Windows
parts:
On 1/13/12 4:49 PM, Daniel Lee wrote:
> For test/gm/parser:
> 1) g++ 4.7.0 experimental runs the test at -O3! Yay!

Thanks for going in today and checking, Daniel.
Great news that it's finally working

To bring everyone else up to date, we haven't
been able to get the Stan parser (the thing
that reads the Stan files and generates a data
structure corresponding to the program) to build
under Windows. Daniel and I have spent dozens of
hours working on the code, searching, trying different
compilers, etc., all to no avail.

I wrote a couple of messages to the developer mailing
list for Boost, built them a standalone test, and a
couple of their developers got back to me -- the
bottom-line is that it still won't compile with
-O0, but it will compile with -O3, which is fine
for production. Go figure (though you'll have to
be a template yoga master to figure this one out).

With -O0 under GNU, it either blows out memory in the
compile, generates a suspect .o file, or crashes the GNU
assembler (the assemblers converts some abstract representation
of the program into more concrete machine code per platform).
The Boost guys looked into it and concluded it's a bug
in the Windows GNU assembler.

One of Boost's taglines is "torturing compilers since
1999".

- Bob

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: finally building on Windows
parts:
Ran into another snag.

GoogleTest crashes when trying to output to an xml file under g++
4.7.0 experimental. I've verified that this doesn't happen under the
older compiler (g++ 4.5.2).

I'm going to check in a new makefile for use for Jenkins. Hopefully
we'll be able to ditch that one day in the future when g++ 4.7 is
stable.


Daniel
